## 2.0.0 (unreleased)

Not released yet: 2.0 ships with the other plugins' rewrites, once they've all run on our own servers (ROADMAP.md, Release). Until then 1.0.1 is the release, and 1.x gets its fixes.

The rewrite: the same commands, flags, permissions, settings and punishments as 1.0.1, now on **Paper, Folia, Spigot and CraftBukkit from 1.8.8 to 26.3**, **Fabric 1.20.1, 1.21.11 and 26.3** (server-side: players install nothing), and **Velocity and BungeeCord**, with xBans' messages and ban screens in eight languages. Keep the 1.0.1 jar to go back to.

### New

- **Bans for the whole network, at the proxy.** With xBans on Velocity or BungeeCord sharing the servers' MySQL database, a banned player is turned away as they log in and never reaches a server; a ban scoped to one server keeps them off that one. A ban or kick made on any server takes the player off the network at once. If the database can't be read, nobody gets in until it can: xBans fails closed, and says so. See [Networks](https://plugins.xenastudios.co/xbans/networks/).
- **Imports from AdvancedBan**, beside LiteBans, EssentialsX and the server's own lists: `/xbans import advancedban`.
- **LiteBans and AdvancedBan import from their own files too**, not only from MySQL or MariaDB: LiteBans' H2 database (`litebans.mv.db`, from any LiteBans version) and AdvancedBan's HSQLDB files (`data/storage.*`). xBans downloads the driver the file needs the first time, reads a copy, and leaves the plugin's files as they were. See [Switching](https://plugins.xenastudios.co/xbans/switching/).
- **`/xbans forget <player>`** deletes the IPs and name xBans keeps for a player, for an erasure request. Their punishments stay: see [Privacy](https://plugins.xenastudios.co/xbans/privacy/#deleting-a-players-data).
- **`/xbans debug`** writes a report to share when asking for help.
- **zChat reads xBans' mutes**, so a muted player can't chat or `/msg` through zChat either, on every server of a network.
- **Ban screens in the player's language**, the one they last played in, as every other message.
- **A staff layer in the API** for vanish and moderation plugins: who's staff, staff notifications (with an event that can change who hears them), silent punishments.

### Upgrading from 1.x

Replace the jar and restart. Your `config.yml` is carried forward and the old one is kept beside it as `config.yml.bak-v1`; your punishments, history and IP records stay where they are (`punishments.db`, or your MySQL tables), untouched: 2.0 reads and writes them exactly as 1.x does. See [Upgrading from 1.x](https://plugins.xenastudios.co/xbans/upgrade/).

- **Messages are in `lang/` now**, one file per language, no longer in `config.yml`; the ban screens and broadcasts too. Every message you changed in 1.x is copied into `lang/en.yml` on the first start, and then xBans sends English to everyone (`messages.language: en`), as 1.x did. Set it to `auto` to give each player their own language.
- **`theme` moved into `messages.theme`**, shared with the other Xena plugins in `plugins/Xena/config.yml` unless you set it here. Colours you changed in 1.x stay xBans' own.
- The error messages (`messages.error.*`) are the core's now: `core.command.*` in `lang/`. "No player named Alex is online" reads "No player called Alex is online" unless you'd changed it.
- `update-checker` is `updates` now: `update-checker.enabled` is carried to `updates.check`.
- **Going back to 1.0.1:** stop the server, put the 1.0.1 jar back, and rename `config.yml.bak-v1` to `config.yml` (keep 2.0's as `config.yml.v2`). Your punishments need nothing: 1.0.1 reads the database as 2.0 left it. If you don't rename the config, 1.0.1 still starts and keeps every setting, with its own default messages.

### For developers: the API's breaking changes

- `XBans.api()` replaces `XBansApi.get()`; it's in Bukkit's services manager as before. Players are `PlayerRef`s (by UUID), so one API works on every platform and the proxies: from Java, `PlayerRefs.of(player.getUniqueId())`.
- `activeBan` and `activeMute` return the punishment or `null` rather than an `Optional`; `punish` and `pardon` (which replaces `revoke`) complete with a `PunishResult` saying how it ended, rather than failing; `PunishRequest.withDurationMillis` replaces `withDuration`.
- The events are xBans' own, on `api.getEvents()` (`PunishEvent`, `PunishedEvent`, `PardonEvent`, `PardonedEvent`, `LoginDeniedEvent`, `StaffNotifyEvent`, each with its `TYPE`), and on Bukkit also Bukkit events in `co.xenastudios.xbans.api.bukkit` (`BukkitPunishEvent` and the rest), which replace 1.x's. `RevokedEvent` is `PardonedEvent`.

## 1.0.1

### Fixed

- While Modrinth is still reviewing xBans, the update checker asks GitHub for its releases instead, so you hear about new versions either way. It sends GitHub only xBans' version, as it does Modrinth.

## 1.0.0

The first release. Drop the jar in and start the server: punishments are kept in SQLite in its own folder, with nothing to set up. Coming from LiteBans, EssentialsX or vanilla bans? `/xbans import <source>`.

### Punishing

- `/ban`, `/tempban`, `/ipban`, `/tempipban`, `/mute`, `/tempmute`, `/ipmute`, `/tempipmute`, `/warn` and `/kick`, and `/unban`, `/unmute` and `/unwarn` by name, uuid, IP or `#id`.
- LiteBans' flags: `-s` silent, `-S` extra silent, `-p` public, `-g` global, `-I` by IP, `server:<name>`, and `--` before a reason that looks like a flag.
- LiteBans' durations: `30m`, `1d2h`, `1.5h`, `2mo`, `1y`, `5 days`, `perm`.
- Templates with escalation ladders (`/ban Steve hacking`: 7 days, then 30, then permanent), each with its own permission (`xbans.template.<name>`), and commands the console runs at a number of warnings. `/tempban` and `/tempmute` never reach a ladder's permanent step.
- Staff limits: weights (`xbans.weight.<n>`), exempt players, and the longest ban and mute per group, templates' durations included (`xbans.limit.bypass-templates` lifts that). An IP ban is held to every account on the IP.
- Unbans follow weights too: staff lift their own punishments and those given by staff with no higher a weight; `xbans.unban.override` lifts any. Imported punishments count as the console's, since their staff's weights aren't known.
- A new ban or mute replaces one on the same server only if it lasts at least as long, reaches everyone the old one did, and its sender could lift the old one: an account ban never lifts an IP ban, and a helper never swaps a senior's ban for their own. Re-banning with the same length changes the reason.
- Replaces vanilla `/ban`, `/pardon`, `/ban-ip`, `/pardon-ip`, `/kick` and `/banlist`.

### Enforcing

- Every ban and mute in force is kept in memory and loaded before anyone can join. Bans are checked at login, again as the connection finishes, and at join, so a ban made while someone connects still catches them.
- Mutes block chat (the older chat events too, so a script or Discord bridge listening there relays nothing, even one that starts listening long after startup), the commands in `mutes.blocked-commands` by any alias or namespace, signs, books and anvil renames.
- A ban screen with the reason, time left and your appeal link.

### Looking up

- `/history`, `/staffhistory`, `/checkban`, `/checkmute`, `/warnings`, `/banlist`, `/mutelist`, `/alts` and `/iphistory`, clickable and paged; `/prunehistory` to delete what's no longer in force.
- Staff are told when a banned player tries to join, or a player joins who shares an IP with a banned account.

### Storage, networks and privacy

- SQLite or MySQL/MariaDB. Punishments are never changed or deleted: an unban is recorded beside the ban.
- Network mode: servers sharing a MySQL database share bans within seconds, and kick a banned player from whichever server they're on. A server that misses a change catches up by reading what's in force again, and keeps trying every 15 seconds while the database is down.
- IPs can be stored as salted hashes (`ips.hash`), or not at all (`ips.enabled: false`). Turning hashing on hashes everything stored in one go, imports' records included. A hashed database won't open without its salt; if the salt is lost for good, `reset-ip-salt.txt` starts over with a new one. Broadcasts and ban lists show half an address at most.
- Imports from LiteBans (MySQL or MariaDB), the server's ban lists and EssentialsX. Players online who are banned by an import are kicked.
- A developer API: check bans and mutes from memory, punish and revoke, read history, and punishment events.
